query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing particle velocity using the HVAF-i7 torch will overcome the thickness limitation of FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with a size range of 15–45 μm
generation.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 torch, with a spray distance optimized for the M3 system (300 or 350 mm) and potentially adjusted for the i7 torch
generation.structural_mediator: Particle velocity and resulting kinetic energy upon impact
generation.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases deposition efficiency, leading to thicker coatings
generation.predicted_outcome: Thicker, adherent bond coats with minimal as-sprayed oxidation and retained coating integrity during high-temperature thermal-barrier service
generation.baseline: 15–45 μm feedstock coatings produced with the HVAF-i7 torch at standard conditions
generation.boundary: Internal diameters as small as 120 mm, high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions
generation.uncertainty: Optimal spray distance for the HVAF-i7 torch, potential effects of increased particle velocity on coating microstructure and properties

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled deposition experiment using the HVAF-i7 torch with varied particle velocities, measuring coating thickness and properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If increasing particle velocity does not result in significantly thicker coatings (>20% increase) without compromising adhesion or oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
